M1_R_distribution.description: Per-pair density ratios R = canonical_density / weighted_density across 21 task-definition pairs
M1_R_distribution.summary: R varies substantially across pairs (CV=0.68). The ratio spans a 17x range from 0.0055 (DEF-FORM-ONLY on listing) to 0.0943 (DEF-FULL-MAP on detail_pet_camera). Variation is driven primarily by definition choice (DEF-FORM-ONLY vs others) and secondarily by task type.

M2_R_by_task_type.summary: Detail tasks have highest mean R (0.064), cart intermediate (0.053), listing lowest (0.036). Separation ratio 1.78x (detail/listing). Task-type explains 14.4% of ratio variance (eta^2=0.144).

M3_R_by_definition.summary: DEF-FORM-ONLY produces ratios ~10x lower than DEF-FULL-MAP and ISOLATED-A-LINK. This is because DEF-FORM-ONLY captures nearly all elements (inForm=true for 17-19/20 elements), making weighted density very high (0.98-0.995) while canonical density remains low.

M4_Spearman_R_canonical.interpretation: Moderate negative correlation between R and canonical density. As canonical density increases, ratio decreases. Not significant at alpha=0.05 due to small N=21.

M5_Spearman_R_weighted.interpretation: Strong negative correlation between R and weighted density (p=0.0016). As weighted density increases, ratio decreases. This is expected: R = canonical/weighted, so higher weighted denominator reduces R.

M6_eta_squared_R_page_type.interpretation: Page type explains 14.4% of ratio variance. Below 0.20 threshold but non-trivial. The ratio captures some task-type structure.

M7_eta_squared_weighted_page_type.interpretation: Weighted density alone explains nearly 0% of ratio variance via page type. The ratio adds substantial task-type information that weighted density alone lacks.

M8_threshold_analysis.interpretation: Threshold T=0.0297 separates pairs into two groups with significantly different weighted density distributions (p=0.001). The lower group (R < 0.03) contains mostly DEF-FORM-ONLY pairs; the upper group contains DEF-FULL-MAP and ISOLATED-A-LINK pairs.

M9_ratio_bimodality.interpretation: No evidence of bimodality (p=0.95). The ratio distribution is unimodal but skewed, with DEF-FORM-ONLY pairs forming a low-R cluster and DEF-FULL-MAP/ISOLATED-A-LINK forming a higher-R cluster.

M10_ratio_range.interpretation: The ratio spans a 17x range, confirming substantial variation across task-definition pairs.

M11_task_type_separation.interpretation: Max inter-group mean ratio / min inter-group mean ratio = 1.78. Task type produces moderate but non-negligible separation in ratio space.

PC1_KNOWN_REVERSAL_PAIRS.description: The 3 task-type groups show different mean ratios if the ratio captures recipe sensitivity
PC1_KNOWN_REVERSAL_PAIRS.expected: Ratio differs across listing, detail, and cart groups
PC1_KNOWN_REVERSAL_PAIRS.observed: Listing mean R=0.036, detail mean R=0.064, cart mean R=0.053. Groups differ (not identical).

NC1_SHUFFLED_RATIO.description: Shuffled canonical values should lose task-type structure in the ratio
NC1_SHUFFLED_RATIO.observed: Real eta^2=0.144, shuffled mean eta^2=0.117. Real > shuffled but difference is modest (NC1 does not pass its strict criterion).

B1_DEGENERATE_DOMINANCE.description: 2-recipe dominance baseline: all 21 pairs degenerate 0%/100%, zero discrimination
B1_DEGENERATE_DOMINANCE.observed: Confirmed from parent experiments. Ratio approach provides continuous discrimination replacing degenerate binary.

B3_CANONICAL_ONLY_BINARY.description: Binary threshold on canonical density alone (all 21 pairs flagged since canonical < 0.01)
B3_CANONICAL_ONLY_BINARY.observed: Canonical densities range 0.0004-0.009. All below any reasonable threshold. Zero specificity.

observations.description: The density ratio R = canonical/weighted varies 17x across 21 task-definition pairs (min 0.0055, max 0.0943, CV=0.68). The ratio is NOT a universal constant — it depends on both the task type and the definition.

Definition choice is the primary driver of ratio variation: DEF-FORM-ONLY pairs have mean R=0.007 (10x lower) while DEF-FULL-MAP and ISOLATED-A-LINK have mean R=0.072 and 0.071 respectively. This is because DEF-FORM-ONLY captures nearly all elements (17-19/20), making weighted density very high (~0.98-0.995) while canonical density remains low.

Task type explains 14.4% of ratio variance (eta^2=0.144). Detail tasks have highest mean R (0.064), cart intermediate (0.053), listing lowest (0.036). The ratio captures task-type structure that weighted density alone misses (eta^2 of weighted density on page_type is nearly 0).

R correlates strongly negatively with weighted density (Spearman rho=-0.707, p=0.0016). This is partially mathematical: R = canonical/weighted, so higher weighted denominator reduces R. However, the ratio adds task-type information beyond weighted density alone.

A threshold T=0.0297 separates pairs into two groups with significantly different weighted density distributions (Kruskal-Wallis p=0.0013). The lower group (R < 0.03) contains 7 DEF-FORM-ONLY pairs; the upper group contains 14 DEF-FULL-MAP and ISOLATED-A-LINK pairs.

The ratio distribution is unimodal (Hartigan dip p=0.95), not bimodal. The apparent two-cluster structure (DEF-FORM-ONLY vs others) is a consequence of definition choice, not natural recipe-sensitivity bimodality.

validity_notes.note: Results are bounded to truncated-first-20 locatable_sample (7 tasks, 1 Magento site, 3 definitions). The locatable_sample is capped at 20 elements per task (actual locatable_elements are 21-82). Full DOM enumeration may change density values and ratios.

The canonical recipe density is computed as (matching_count * 0.5) / elements_with_bbox, which is the expected value under p=0.5 independent Bernoulli inclusion. This is deterministic given the data. A single stochastic realization would show variance but the expected value is exact.

The weighted recipe density is computed as sum(element_area / total_area) for matching elements. This uses the area-weighted formula from the spec, not the role-based weighted sampling from the null model in prior experiments. The absolute density values may differ from prior experiments that used different weighted recipes.

NC1 (null control) does not pass its strict criterion: real eta^2=0.144 vs shuffled mean eta^2=0.117. The difference is positive (real > shuffled) but modest. This suggests the task-type structure in R is weak relative to the definition-driven structure.
Small N (21 pairs) limits statistical power. Spearman correlations have wide confidence intervals. The eta-squared for page_type (0.144) has low precision with only 3 groups and N=21.

The ratio metric R = canonical/weighted conflates two sources of variation: (a) task-type-dependent differences in element composition, and (b) definition-dependent differences in which elements match. The 10x ratio difference between DEF-FORM-ONLY and DEF-FULL-MAP is primarily a definition artifact, not task-type sensitivity.
